title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All Directors of the Company; distinguished for clearance (approval of the Chairman, or for the Chairman's own trades, another non-executive Director nominated by the Board).

tiers.name: Senior Management
tiers.description: The Managing Director, the Chief Financial Officer, the Company Secretary, and all senior executives; distinguished for clearance (approval of the Managing Director) and a post-trade disclosure duty to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: others
tiers.description: All other executives and employees of the Company not within Directors or Senior Management; distinguished for clearance (approval of the Company Secretary).

tiers.name: associates
tiers.description: Family members, or a trust or company over which a covered person has influence or control; may not be used to trade in circumstances where the covered person would themselves have been prohibited from trading.

windows.start_anchor: 15 January following the end of the previous December quarter
windows.end_anchor: two (2) business days after the day on which the Company releases its December quarterly cash flow report

windows.start_anchor: 15 April following the end of the previous March quarter
windows.end_anchor: two (2) business days after the day on which the Company releases its March quarterly cash flow report

windows.start_anchor: 15 July following the end of the previous June quarter
windows.end_anchor: two (2) business days after the day on which the Company releases its June quarterly cash flow report

windows.start_anchor: 15 October following the end of the previous September quarter
windows.end_anchor: two (2) business days after the day on which the Company releases its September quarterly cash flow report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, the Managing Director or the Company Secretary may implement a black out period with immediate effect via written notification (generally distributed by e-mail) from the Company Secretary. Not stated as confidential: the notification is distributed to those covered and the Company Secretary will communicate in writing the lifting of a black out period.

rules.detail: 'Securities covered' is defined as all securities issued by the Company, including ordinary shares and options; there is no mention of third-party derivative products (such as a bank's OTC put or call) over those securities, and no dealing definition broad enough to plainly sweep them in.
No concept of hedging or limiting economic risk appears anywhere in the policy, for vested or unvested holdings.
Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards are not addressed, and 'deal in securities' is not defined to include agreements to deal.
Short selling is not mentioned; only a general ban on trading for short term or speculative gain applies.

Margin lending is named only as an example within the excluded-trading clause: a forced sale by a secured lender exercising their rights is excluded from the black-out restrictions. Entering into the margin loan itself, or granting security over the shares for it, is not otherwise regulated by the policy (no clearance requirement, unlike some peer policies).
rules.evidence: a disposal of Company shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over securities is not defined as 'dealing' and is not otherwise addressed, beyond the passing reference to margin lending in the excluded-trading clause.

Secured financing generally is addressed only through the margin lending example in the excluded-trading clause; entering into any secured financing arrangement is not otherwise restricted or made subject to clearance.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Company shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Trading outside a black-out period is only permitted if it is not for short-term or speculative gain, and clearance to trade during a black-out period will only be given if the approver is satisfied the transaction is not for speculative gain; no numeric holding period or LIFO basis is specified.
rules.evidence: A person covered by this Policy may trade in securities at any time but only if: there is no black out period in place; and they have no Inside Information; and the trading is not for short term or speculative gain.

clearance.approver: the Chairman, or in the case of a proposed trade by the Chairman, another non-executive Director nominated by the Board for the purpose
clearance.evidence: in the case of Directors – they have obtained the approval of the Chairman or in the case of any proposed trade by the Chairman, of another non-executive Director nominated by the Board for the purpose... If approval is given, the trade must be executed within 2 business days of the approval.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days following each transaction
clearance.evidence: In the case of Senior Management – they have obtained the approval of the Managing Director ... Senior Management must advise the Company Secretary in writing of the details of completed transactions within 2 business days following each transaction.
In the case of others - they have obtained the approval of the Company Secretary.

short_term.evidence: the trading is not for short term or speculative gain.

exceptions.approver: the relevant approving person (Chairman, Managing Director or Company Secretary depending on tier)
exceptions.evidence: ‘severe financial hardship’ could include (but is not limited to) the applicant having a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Company shares.

exceptions.approver: the relevant approving person (Chairman, Managing Director or Company Secretary depending on tier)
exceptions.evidence: ‘exceptional circumstances’ could include (but is not limited to) where the applicant is required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings, for example, in a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell Company shares or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for him or her to do so.
transfers of securities already held from a person's own name into a superannuation fund of which that person is a beneficiary and vice versa.
an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.
trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most members such as a rights issue or a share purchase plan.
a disposal of Company shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
trading under any employee incentive scheme in accordance with the rules of a Board approved Incentive Plan.
a new issue where the issue is available pro rata to all holders of securities of the relevant class.
an executive or employee share or option plan.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or, for the Chairman's own trades, a Board-nominated non-executive Director), the Managing Director (for Senior Management), or the Company Secretary (for others) may approve trading during a black-out period only where the applicant is in severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances exist (e.g. court order, court-enforceable undertaking, or other legal/regulatory requirement), and only if satisfied there is no undisclosed inside information and the trade would not be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair. Approval must be in writing and the trade executed within 2 business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons covered by this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or though a trust or company over which they have influence or control, in circumstances where they would have been prohibited from trading in their own name.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family member, trust or controlled company does not escape the black-out or clearance restrictions that would otherwise apply to the executive personally.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No provision requires clearance to enter into a margin loan or grant security over shares, and the resulting enforcement sale is excluded trading; the loan leg of a funded collar therefore falls into an unregulated gap rather than being expressly permitted or barred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to all securities issued by the Company from time to time, including ordinary shares and options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because 'securities covered' is limited to securities issued by the Company, a bank-written OTC put and call over the shares arguably fall outside the defined scope of this policy altogether, creating interpretive uncertainty as to whether the derivative legs of the collar are caught at all (as distinct from any subsequent dealing in the underlying shares).

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval is given, the trade must be executed within 2 business days of the approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade in the underlying shares (e.g. delivery on unwind) must be executed within 2 business days of approval or fresh clearance is required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Permission will be given for trading pursuant to this section 4 only after a written request for approval is provided ... and only if the approving person is satisfied that the transaction would not be ... seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where hardship or exceptional circumstances are shown, a bespoke bank collar entered during a black-out period could still be refused if perceived as unfair, adding discretionary approval risk beyond the strict legal tests.

summary: A funded collar sits largely outside the express terms of this policy, which creates both opportunity and uncertainty. 'Securities covered' is limited to shares and options issued by the Company, so a bank's OTC put and call may fall outside the policy's defined scope altogether; if treated as caught, they would need to be dealt with as an ordinary 'dealing' requiring approval (Chairman for Directors, Managing Director for Senior Management, Company Secretary for others) only if entered during a black-out period, executed within 2 business days, and not for short-term or speculative gain. The loan leg is effectively unregulated: no clearance is required to enter a margin loan or grant security over the shares, and a forced sale by the bank as secured lender is expressly excluded trading even during a black-out period. Because the policy is silent rather than clearly permissive on derivatives and secured financing, the bank should seek the Company's own confirmation that the structure is acceptable, structure entry, roll and unwind of the underlying share position outside the four quarterly black-out windows, and route any executive or family-entity involvement consistently with the anti-avoidance clause in section 2.3.
